messages:
Anya (PM): quick sync — sales asked for a high-throughput add-on we can sell to ecommerce partners. sketching a small proposal below, want input on launch criteria and contract guardrails.
Maria (Product Finance): :eyes: can you paste the numbers? need expected rev uplift + cost delta.
Anya (PM): rough: add-on named 'priority-throughput' — priced as a % uplift + per-minute SLA credit. tiers: 10k, 50k, 200k reqs/day. soft-limit with throttled burst. expected 20–30% rev uplift for pilot customers.
Sam (Sales): customer ACME asked for sustained 1000 rps with 99.9% p95 latency < 250ms. they'd pay for predictability. they want explicit overage rules though.
Kevin (Legal): high-level constraints: no hard unlimited SLA in initial release. need overage cap, liability carveouts, and a clear termination/rollback clause. also require logging/audit for compliance.
Jasper (Eng): technical questions: how do we guarantee 1000 rps? do we map to dedicated pools or priority scheduling on shared pools? opt: dedicated lanes (higher cost) vs priority Q within same pool (cheaper but noisier).
Anya (PM): initial thought: implement as "priority lane" that routes to reserved backends for the top tier, and to preemptible priority scheduling for mid-tier. fallback model for capacity shortage. need canary path in routing.
Maria (Product Finance): pricing model options: (A) fixed monthly seat + usage uplift; (B) flat % surcharge on tokens for prioritized requests; (C) commitment tiers with rollback credits on SLA misses. Which aligns ops best?
Jasper (Eng): prefer (C) for predictability and capacity planning. credits on SLA miss are simpler than real-time throttles from infra POV.
Sam (Sales): sales prefer (A) for enterprise buyers (easy to forecast). mid-market prefers (B). we could offer both but need clear packaging rules.
Kevin (Legal): contract language we want: define "priority requests" via route tag, cap soft/hard, overage pricing at 1.5x standard, and automatic fallback to best-effort if we can't satisfy SLA during incidents. also require a 30-day notice for removal of dedicated capacity.
Anya (PM): launch criteria proposal (draft):
- Implementation: routing + reserved pool for tier N, console controls to opt-in/out, per-route tagging.
- Observability: per-request priority label, cost/latency breakdown, alerting for >5% SLA breach in 1h.
- Billing: clear invoice line items + overage calc + crediting flow tested end-to-end.
- Legal: standard contract template + overage and rollback language approved.
- Pilot: 3 customers (1 enterprise, 2 midsize), 6 week pilot, success if avg p95 meets target and no >10% cost overshoot.
Maria (Product Finance): add: projected unit economics spreadsheet and sensitivity to 30/50/80% utilization. i'll own the model.
Jasper (Eng): engineering unknowns: autoscaler behavior for reserved pools, eviction policy, prefix caching impact under priority lane, and load tests needed. estimate 4 sprints to get safe pilot infra.
Sam (Sales): timeline: if we start now we can offer pilot to ACME and 2 inbound pilots in Q3. need marketing collateral and pricing sheet.
Anya (PM): decision needed: (1) dual-pricing (A+B) vs commitment-only (C), (2) whether to require dedicated capacity for top tier, (3) pilot gating metrics. please reply with votes.
Maria (Product Finance): vote: (C) commitment-first, allow (A) for enterprise negotiation.
Sam (Sales): vote: dual-pricing — offer A to enterprise, B for self-serve midsize, C as discounted commitment.
Kevin (Legal): vote: require dedicated for top tier, but allow software fallback. legal ok with draft language once product writes it up.
Jasper (Eng): vote: require dedicated for top tier, otherwise we won't meet latency guarantees.
ops-bot: deploy-bot notice: load-test cluster scheduled at 2024-09-10T20:00Z for priority-lane canary (job #5543).
Anya (PM): thanks — next actions: Maria to own unit-econ, Jasper to draft infra runbook and time estimate, Kevin to propose contract snippet, Sam to line up pilots. I'll consolidate and post an updated spec by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
